jobs.title: Senior IT Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Alloy is where you belong!
 Alloy is the AI-powered identity and fraud prevention platform that accelerates onboarding, stops fraud, and scales compliance across the customer lifecycle so financial organizations can grow without limits. More than 900 of the world's leading financial institutions and fintechs trust Alloy for smarter risk management that drives growth.
 Through our values: Be Bold, Go Fast, Collaborate, and Celebrate Our Differences, we are creating a workplace where you can grow, thrive, and belong.
 See how we've been continuously recognized and named one of Inc. Magazine's Best Workplaces , Forbes America's Best Startup Employers , Best Fintech to Work for by American Banker, year after year.
 Check out our investors and read more about us here .
 About the team
 The IT and Security team controls who and what can reach Alloy's systems, from the laptops our people use to the SaaS tools and AI agents they work in. Our customers are banks and fintechs, and our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 programs depend on access controls that hold up under audit. We run as a shared-responsibility team: each engineer is the go-to expert in their area and backs up teammates across the rest.
 Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. Given the internal client-facing nature of this role, the in-person office attendance requirement is four days per week (Tuesday-Thursday, with your choice on whether the fourth in-person day is Monday or Friday).
 What you'll do
 You'll own workforce identity at Alloy, from how access is granted and automated to how it is reviewed and removed. You'll be the primary expert for Okta, SaaS access, and identity automation while sharing coverage for broader IT and Security work.
 IAM and Okta Administration: Serve as the primary technical SME for workforce identity and access management, including Okta groups, policies, application assignments, admin roles, MFA, and authentication controls.
 SaaS Access and Integrations: Manage SaaS access and application onboarding. Implement and maintain SSO integrations using SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning, and Google Workspace access.
 Identity Lifecycle and Automation: Maintain and improve employee and contractor joiner/mover/leaver workflows from our HRIS through our IdP and downstream SaaS. Use Okta Workflows and other automation to cut manual access processes.
 Access Operations: Troubleshoot authentication and provisioning issues, administer temporary access and exceptions, and make access requests more reliable and efficient.
 RBAC Management: Refine, manage, and evolve Alloy's approach to role and attribute based access control.
 Privileged Access Management: Mature PAM/TPAM for administrator and production resource access, including just-in-time and temporary access and break-glass procedures.
 Non-Human Identity Management: Improve ownership and lifecycle controls for service accounts, system users, API credentials and tokens, OAuth applications, bots, and integrations.
 AI Identity and Access: Shape identity and delegated-access controls for AI platforms, AI agents, and MCP integrations, including the scope of access available to tools and agents.
 Access Governance and Compliance: Strengthen least privilege and RBAC/ABAC, run access and privileged-access reviews, remediate stale or orphaned accounts, enforce contractor access expiration, and provide IAM evidence for ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
 Shared IT/Security Engineering: Take on endpoint security, EDR, DLP, application control, email security, SaaS/security tools, and other IT/Security projects within a shared-SME and backup-coverage model.
 Incident Response and Collaboration: Investigate incidents involving identity, users, endpoints, email, and SaaS. Coordinate with teammates and business partners, and keep processes and documentation clear.
 On-call Rotation: Join the IT and Security on-call rotation, responding to critical alerts and urgent after-hours support requests.
 What we're looking for
 Must-haves:
 Hands-on experience in IT or security engineering, with significant responsibility for Okta or a comparable workforce identity provider
 Experience administering IdP groups, access and authentication policies, SaaS application assignments, MFA, and administrative roles
 Experience implementing and troubleshooting SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM provisioning, and OAuth-based integrations
 Experience running employee and contractor identity lifecycles across HR systems, an IdP, Google Workspace, and downstream SaaS applications
 Ability to automate access workflows using Okta Workflows, APIs, scripts, or comparable tools
 Understanding of least privilege, RBAC/ABAC, access reviews, and account lifecycle controls
 Working familiarity with endpoint security, EDR, DLP, email security, and SaaS security tooling, and willingness to work beyond IAM
 Strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills in a shared-responsibility IT/Security team
 Nice-to-haves:

jobs.title: Strategic Partner Director, Channel Sales
jobs.description:
WHY SOCURE?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Socure's mission is to verify 100% of good identities in real time and eliminate identity fraud across the digital economy. We're hiring a Strategic Partner Director, Channel Sales, to build and grow the partnerships that bring Socure to banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions.

You'll own Socure's most important channel relationships in financial services, including core banking providers, digital banking and account-opening platforms, banking-as-a-service providers, and systems integrators. You'll act as the connective tissue between partners and Socure's Sales, Product, Marketing, and Legal teams, turning partnerships into a repeatable source of revenue.

This is a senior, quota-carrying role for a partnerships leader who knows how financial institutions buy technology and who can build trust at the executive level. You'll own partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue and shape how Socure scales across the financial services market.





WHAT YOU'LL DO


PARTNER STRATEGY & DEVELOPMENT

 - Define and execute a channel strategy for financial services that identifies the partners, partnership models, and target segments that will drive the most revenue.

 - Recruit, negotiate, and close new strategic partnerships, including referral, reseller, embedded, and OEM agreements, in partnership with Legal and Finance.

 - Own and grow relationships with Socure's most important financial services partners, building trust at the executive, product, and sales levels.

 - Build joint business plans with each strategic partner, with clear revenue targets, target accounts, integration milestones, and go-to-market commitments.


CHANNEL SALES & PIPELINE

 - Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue targets for financial services.

 - Run joint account planning and co-selling with partner sales teams to win new banks, credit unions, and fintechs.

 - Partner with Socure Account Executives to bring partners into direct deals where they add value, and manage deal registration and channel conflict fairly.

 - Maintain accurate partner pipeline, forecasts, and activity in Salesforce, and report on channel performance to sales leadership.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP

 - Work with Product and Engineering to prioritize and deliver partner integrations that make Socure easy to buy and deploy through each platform.

 - Partner with Marketing on joint campaigns, events, content, and co-branded materials that build demand with partners' customer bases.

 - Train partner sales and solutions teams on Socure's products, value propositions, and ideal customer profile so they can position Socure with confidence.

 - Bring partner feedback, market insights, and competitive intelligence into Socure's product and go-to-market planning.

 - Establish and track KPIs tied to partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced revenue, partner activation, and deal velocity.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years of enterprise sales or business development experience, with at least 5 years in channel sales, strategic alliances, or partnerships at a financial services technology company.

 - A track record of meeting or exceeding partner-sourced revenue targets and closing complex, multi-party deals.

 - An established network across banks, credit unions, and the technology providers that serve them, such as core banking, digital banking, and banking-as-a-service platforms.

 - Experience negotiating partnership agreements, including referral, reseller, embedded, and OEM models.

 - The ability to explain complex, data-driven technology in clear business terms to partner and customer executives.

 - Experience working closely with product, marketing, legal, and sales teams, and influencing cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority.

 - Analytical rigor and comfort building partner business cases, forecasts, and performance reporting.

 - Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple strategic partners and deals at once in a fast-moving environment.

 - Bonus: experience selling identity verification, fraud prevention, KYC/AML, or RegTech solutions, or experience building a channel program from the ground up.

Expert Insights, which spans AlphaSense’s Expert Transcript Library and 1x1 Call Services offerings,  delivers a new and transformative form of market intelligence content. Through transcripts covering thousands of companies, it captures the unfiltered views and insights of business operators in the trenches, interviewed by professional investors who drill into key questions on what’s truly important about a company at each moment in time. AlphaSense’s library of over 220,000 transcripts is the market’s largest, covering all sectors of the economy, with thousands more published each month. Expert Insights is quickly becoming a table-stakes solution for institutional investors to choose the right companies to invest in while gaining rapid adoption among all other consumers of market intelligence from sell-side research and banking, consultancies, and large corporations.

The Directed Content team is responsible for identifying, recruiting, and onboarding the best possible experts from around the world based on the targets and topics we are looking to generate content against - ensuring that the interviews with those experts are of the highest-possible quality and relevance.

 Reporting to the Sector Lead, Directed Content, our Project Managers are the process and project management lynchpins of the Directed Content engine - responsible for defining the research scope and angles of Directed Content projects that guide the work of our Analysts. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
jobs.location: San Francisco; Remote (United States); Toronto; Seattle; New York City
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
jobs.location: San Francisco; Remote (United States); Seattle; New York City
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

 - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

 - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

 - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

We’re looking for a Senior People Systems Analyst to own and scale the systems and workflows that support Harvey’s growing global workforce. This role will primarily focus on Workday HCM, owning the design, configuration, testing, and continuous improvement of complex business processes. You’ll also be the go-to systems expert for Benefits and our Applicant Tracking System (Ashby). That means leading feature evaluation, solution design, configuration, root-cause troubleshooting, and end-to-end testing.

You’ll partner closely with People Operations, Benefits, Recruiting, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and Corporate IT to turn business needs into scalable, intuitive, and well-governed system solutions. The ideal candidate is an experienced, hands-on systems professional who works independently from requirements through deployment, brings a clear point of view on how to solve problems, and influences stakeholders toward durable, scalable outcomes.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the configuration, maintenance, and optimization of Workday HCM, including complex business processes, condition rules, approval routing, notifications, security assignments, and worker lifecycle workflows.

 - Lead solution design end to end: translate ambiguous business needs into system solutions, assess downstream impacts across HCM, Benefits, Payroll, reporting, integrations, and employee experience, and bring recommendations to critical decision points.

 - Serve as the subject-matter expert for Benefits systems, owning plan configuration, eligibility rules, enrollment workflows, vendor integrations, annual enrollment readiness, issue resolution, and process improvements.

 - Support Recruiting Systems and administration which includes integrations, and data quality.

 - Advise senior stakeholders on system capabilities, new features, configuration tradeoffs, and opportunities to simplify or automate manual processes. Explain complex topics clearly and persuasively.

 - Define and drive testing strategy across Workday, Benefits, Ashby, and connected systems, including workflow, regression, release, and user acceptance testing.

 - Diagnose complex or unusual system and data issues by tracing configuration, business rules, integrations, and upstream and downstream dependencies. Identify root causes and put durable fixes in place rather than one-off workarounds.

 - Lead enhancement projects from discovery through deployment with People Operations, Benefits, Recruiting, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and IT, including gathering requirements, documenting options, and prioritizing work.

 - Set the standard for configuration documentation, test plans, process maps, release notes, and operational procedures that support governance and team self-service.

 - Proactively monitor system health and data integrity, lead audit and reconciliation support, and uphold security and data governance practices for employee and candidate data.

 - Lead Workday and vendor release management: evaluate new functionality, assess impact, coordinate testing, and drive adoption decisions.

 - Act as a resource for peers and stakeholders on complex or challenging systems questions, sharing knowledge and best practices across the team.





WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience configuring and supporting Workday, an HRIS, or related enterprise business systems.

 - Deep experience with Workday HCM configuration and the Business Process Framework, including condition rules, approval routing, notifications, security, and workflow design.

 - Proven ability to independently design and deliver complex, cross-system workflows, using sound judgment to know when a decision needs broader review.

 - A track record of owning projects that improved workflows, reduced manual effort, or introduced new tools or automation.

 - Strong experience turning ambiguous business requirements into system solutions, often with limited information, and explaining technical tradeoffs persuasively to non-technical and senior audiences.

 - Experience defining and running testing strategies, including regression, UAT, defect triage, data validation, and production change management.

 - Solid working knowledge of Benefits administration or Benefits systems, including eligibility, enrollment, plan configuration, vendor feeds, and annual enrollment.

 - Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes across systems, processes, integrations, and data.

 - Excellent communication, documentation, and stakeholder management skills, adapting your style to different audiences.

 - Ability to manage competing priorities independently, make well-reasoned recommendations, and operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.


BONUS POINTS

 - Workday certification or Workday Pro certification in HCM, Benefits, or a related area.

 - Experience with Workday integrations, EIBs, reports, calculated fields, or APIs.

 - Experience supporting recruiting system integrations with Workday or other people systems.

 - Experience with Workday Benefits, Absence, Compensation, Payroll, or Recruiting-related processes.

 - Experience supporting global HR systems, multiple worker populations, or international expansion.

 - Experience leading the evaluation and adoption of new Workday or HR technology features.

 - Experience with security configuration, role-based access, audit readiness, or data governance.

 - Experience mentoring or guiding other systems analysts or administrators.

 - Experience working at a high-growth technology company.




HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT

In this role, you’ll own key parts of Harvey’s people systems foundation and help make sure it is reliable, scalable, and easy to use. You’ll improve the employee and candidate experience by removing manual work, strengthening data quality, and helping People teams operate with greater confidence. Your expertise will shape how HCM, Benefits, and recruiting workflows evolve as Harvey grows, and you’ll set the standards for how we design, test, and govern changes to our systems.





COMPENSATION

$136,000 - $204,000 USD

ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey's Finance Engineering team is the investment-side counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: former investment professionals who bring real deal experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Forward Deployed Finance Engineers lead discovery, demos, pilots, trainings, onboarding, and custom builds alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real investment work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark. Harvey Deals is where investment teams run their deals — screening, underwriting, diligence, and committee materials — built in the firm's own templates and formats, with every figure traceable back to the document it came from. Harvey works with 150+ asset management firms and analyzes 178M+ documents each month; the Finance Engineering team is how that capability meets the way deal teams actually work.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need. It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.

This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit. You will build the credit playbook — demo library, workflow templates, use cases — while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.

You may be asked to travel around 2–3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1–3 days at a time.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with direct lenders, opportunistic and specialty finance managers, BDC managers, and insurer credit arms throughout the pre-sales process and stay with them well past it — leading pilots on live opportunities, guiding lenders through what's possible with AI, and sitting down with credit teams to build screening, underwriting, and credit committee workflows in the firm's own templates and formats.

The work is the work they did on the desk: lender presentation and CIM review; QoE read-throughs and data pack analysis; cash flow and leverage modeling; sizing and structuring; covenant and credit agreement review; credit memo drafting; and comps. It continues post-close into compliance certificate review, covenant tracking, amendment and waiver analysis, and quarterly portfolio reporting, so value compounds after the first deal. Along the way, Finance Engineers bring credit-team feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.







WHAT YOU HAVE




 - 6+ years on the investment or underwriting team at a direct lender, private credit fund, BDC manager, or insurer private credit arm, with demonstrated ownership of live deal work: screening, underwriting, diligence workstreams, modeling, structuring, and drafting credit committee materials. Asset-based and specialty finance backgrounds are welcome. Leveraged finance, restructuring advisory, or rating-agency experience before the principal side is welcome, but principal-side deal execution is required.

 - Strong command of the documents and data that drive a credit decision — lender presentation and CIM, QoE and data pack, model, credit agreement and intercreditor, compliance certificates — and an instinct for where the numbers and the paper disagree.

 - Advanced Excel and financial modeling, comfort with prompting and agentic AI workflows, and a builder's instinct for turning a repeated manual process into a repeatable automation. Python, SQL, or experience building internal tools is a plus.

 - Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility from analysts and associates through to partners and credit committee members.

 - Outstanding communication and presentation skills — comfortable leading a live demo, facilitating a workshop, or holding your own in a technical conversation about a covenant package or an underwriting assumption.

 - Deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform investment work, paired with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset and bias toward action.

 - Track record partnering with senior stakeholders to drive results, with curiosity for testing approaches and optimizing for customer outcomes.

 - Customer-facing or commercial experience (LP or investor relations, capital formation, banking coverage, business development) and/or hands-on experience using AI tools in an investment setting are pluses.

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and deliver production-grade AI agents https://sierra.ai/blog/meet-the-ai-agent-engineer: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.

 - Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-development-life-cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

 - Partner with large enterprises and cutting-edge startups: You’ll work directly with leaders at some of the world’s largest enterprises to understand their most pressing business challenges, and build AI agents that transform how they operate at scale. You'll also partner with the most cutting-edge startups in Silicon Valley, embedding AI agents across their entire business stack to drive innovation and efficiency.

 - Build the future of the platform: Your direct work with customers will guide the evolution of Sierra's core platform. You'll surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform to shape the future of AI agent development and Sierra's product.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are some examples of projects that engineers on our team have worked on recently:

 - Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

 - Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalizing product recommendations

 - Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services!

 - Facilitate design partnerships for new product initiatives, such as new agent architectures, self-service capabilities, and generative agent development

 - Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

 - Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

 - A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

 - Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

 - Excellent communication skills - clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences


EVEN BETTER...

 - Experience building or deploying AI/LLM systems in production

 - Have been a founder or founding engineer - you know what it means to balance craft, ownership, and speed

 - Familiarity with tools that power today's AI agents: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering

 - Prior experience with React, TypeScript, and/or Go

 - Previous roles where you interfaced with customers or led technical projects with external stakeholders


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 - Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


BE YOU, WITH US

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Data Lifecycle
jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it. We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.

This team is core to how Decagon scales. Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems. The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents. A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.

Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.



About the Role

You’ll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted. That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.

You’ll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch. You’ll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you’re building is actually right for them.

Engineers here own features end to end, from technical architecture through deployment and the iteration after it. On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes. An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.



In this role, you will

 - Build PII handling and redaction systems that identify and protect sensitive information across conversations, agent traces, and other customer data

 - Design configuration abstractions for redaction and retention policies that balance enterprise flexibility with clear, safe defaults

 - Build reliable data deletion workflows that propagate across storage systems and derived data, with retries, verification, and visibility into failures

 - Build self-serve tools and APIs that let customers configure, test, and understand their data lifecycle policies without relying on an engineer

 - Build LLM-backed systems that scan and detect data anomalies and violations

 - Train and/or tune models for detecting data of various forms (including PII and PHI)

 - Extend redaction and identification to multimodal agents, including images, attachments, voice notes, and documents.

 - Build monitoring and auditability that make it clear what data was processed, what remains, and where a policy has failed—without exposing sensitive information in the process

 - Handle data lifecycle systems at scale, including backfills, partial failures, and safe rollouts; your work will touch critical flows for Fortune 100 companies
   
   

Your background and skillset look something like this

 - 4+ years building software products, with strong product thinking

 - Proficient in Python, comfortable working across the entire stack

 - Experience designing reliable backend systems and data pipelines, including asynchronous processing, retries, and failure recovery

 - Understanding of what operational maturity looks like for critical systems, including observability and monitoring

 - Complex systems instincts: you can reason about where data flows, where copies persist, and what happens when one part of a workflow fails

 - A high degree of comfort debugging system failures in deep technology stacks, using whatever tool gets you to the answer

 - Judgment about when to ship fast and when correctness, privacy, and irreversible operations require slowing down
   
   

Even better

 - Experience with PII detection, redaction, tokenization, or secure handling of sensitive data

 - Experience building data retention, deletion, or privacy request workflows across multiple storage systems

 - Experience building security-sensitive product systems, such as authentication, authorization, and data access controls

 - Familiarity with privacy and compliance requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, or PCI, and translating them into engineering controls

 - Background with LLMs, evals, or AI agent systems, especially handling sensitive data in model inputs, outputs, and traces

 - Experience with observability, audit trails, or operational tooling for large-scale data systems

 - Work with sensitive data in voice, images, or other non-text formats



Compensation

$200K – $400K + Offers Equity



This range reflects the expected compensation for this role. Compensation within the range is determined based on experience, skills, and the scope of responsibilities, with flexibility for candidates who demonstrate exceptional impact. 



In addition to base salary, we offer competitive equity. Final compensation may vary based on location within the United States.



Benefits

We proudly offer the following benefits for our full-time employees:

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life Insurance and Disability Benefits

 - Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)

 - Parental Leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance

 - Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best

 - Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)

These benefits are described in more detail in Decagon’s policies, may vary by location, and can change at any time according to applicable compensation and benefits plans.

jobs.title: Global Procurement Analyst
jobs.description:
We are an AI company operating at the cutting edge of the industry, growing quickly in a fast-moving environment. As we scale and prepare for a future IPO, we are building our Procurement function from the ground up. This is our first Procurement Analyst role in the company, so you will help define how we buy, not just execute it. Your passion for Procurement will help build and run our source-to-pay processes with strong internal controls, clear segregation of duties between procurement and payment, and audit-ready documentation. This is a global role: you will support stakeholders and suppliers across regions and work closely with the rest of the Procure to Pay (P2P) and Finance teams.
 Key Responsibilities
 Procurement operations
 Manage the end-to-end purchasing operations across all spend categories (software, cloud, professional services, hardware, facilities, and more), from requisition intake and PO issuance in Zip / Coupa.
 Review purchase requests for completeness, budget and policy compliance before approval.
 Issue and track purchase orders, and follow up with suppliers on delivery, pricing, and service levels.
 Support RFQ/RFP processes: gather requirements, solicit/compare bids, and document selection rationale.  Support negotiations and renewals in partnership with Legal and business owners.
 Support requesters across time zones and regions, handling multi-currency and cross-border purchasing needs.
 Controls and audit readiness
 Help design and implement procurement policies, approval matrices (delegation of authority), and procedures aligned with IPO and audit requirements.
 Enforce segregation of duties between procurement (requisition, sourcing, PO creation, vendor selection) and payment (invoice processing, payment execution), in coordination with Accounts Payable and Finance.
 Maintain complete, organized documentation for every purchase (quotes, approvals, contracts, POs) so it is available for internal and external audits.
 Monitor and report on policy exceptions, such as off-contract spend, retroactive POs, and split purchases, and escalate as needed.
 Support internal and external audit requests and help remediate findings.
 Vendor management
 Maintain accurate vendor master data and a centralized vendor and contract repository.
 Run supplier onboarding, including due diligence, documentation, tax compliance validation, and conflict-of-interest checks for domestic and international suppliers.
 Track supplier performance and support periodic vendor reviews using AI and other tools.
 Analysis and reporting
 Use AI to analyze spend data across categories and regions to identify savings opportunities, consolidation potential, and compliance gaps.
 Build regular reports and KPIs, such as spend under management, PO compliance, cycle times, and savings.
 Support budget tracking with Finance and flag potential overruns.
 Process improvement
 Contribute to the implementation and optimization of procurement tools and workflows, particularly Coupa and Zip.
 Document processes and create guidance and training for internal requesters.
 Propose and drive improvements that balance speed with control in a high-growth environment.
 Requirements
 Experience and knowledge
 3+ years of experience in Procurement, Purchasing, or a related P2P function.
 Hands-on experience with Coupa and Zip or other modern procurement and AP tools.
 Familiarity with corporate procurement policies, guidelines, and internal controls.
 Understanding of P2P cycle and basic concepts of segregation of duties and approval workflows.
 Professional fluency in English (written and spoken), as you will primarily support global teams and suppliers.
 Core competencies (non-negotiable)
 Interpersonal skills: builds trusted relationships with stakeholders at all levels and can say “no” or “not like this” constructively.  Strong negotiation and influencing skills.
 Communication skills: communicate clearly, in English writing and verbally, with business teams, suppliers, and senior leaders, and can explain the “why” behind controls.
 Ownership and a bias for action in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.
 Strong attention to detail and a commitment to compliance and integrity.
 Self-management and strong written communication in a remote, cross-time-zone setting.
 Nice to have
 Experience in a high-growth, technology, or SaaS/AI company.

jobs.description:
The Role
 The UK is making a wholesale shift to AI: government, from the AI Opportunities Action Plan through to the tools the Incubator for AI is putting in front of civil servants, and enterprises racing to put AI to work. Scale wants to play a foundational role in building the reliable AI applications both will run on. Our work spans building custom AI applications that reach millions of users, generating high-quality training data for custom LLMs, and providing upskilling and AI advisory services. We're building our UK business from a standing start, and we need someone with a lot of energy to help it move.
 As a Strategist, you'll help grow Scale's UK business, partnering with technical stakeholders to identify and win opportunities across public sector (central government and defence & security) and enterprise. Public sector is the main focus, but we're a small UK team and you'll flex onto enterprise opportunities where they matter. The role is UK-focussed to start, with scope to extend into Europe and the Middle East as the team grows. You'll sit at the centre of our go-to-market effort, combining business development groundwork with the bids and tender work that turns an opportunity into a contract. You'll work in a dynamic and often unstructured environment, and you'll learn how big AI programmes get sold and delivered into government and large organisations, working right next to the people doing it.
 This is a technical, commercially minded role. It's a good fit if you're curious about AI and data, can explain technical ideas in simple, precise language, and want real responsibility early.
 What you'll do
 Work with the UK Public Sector Lead, UK leadership, government relations and the wider team on go-to-market strategy across central government, defence & security, and enterprise
 Research target departments and enterprise accounts, map who matters, and build target lists, outreach and pipeline
 Break into UK enterprise: pick the sectors and accounts worth going after, get in front of commercial buyers, and run deals that sit outside public procurement
 Build relationships and partnerships that open routes to new opportunities, from government and ecosystem partners to delivery and channel partners
 Help customers across government and enterprise find impactful AI use cases and shape their vision for AI
 Run framework applications and tenders end to end (PQQs, RFIs, RFPs), and get to know UK public sector procurement properly (G-Cloud, the Digital Marketplace, the main CCS frameworks)

 Sit in on customer meetings, answer questions as they come up, and turn them into clear next steps that move an opportunity towards a signed deal
 Take on whatever the market needs. Roles are loose when a team is this small.
 What we're looking for
 At least 5 years in business development, bids, consulting, strategy or advisory, ideally with some 0-to-1 or market-entry exposure. Public sector experience is a plus, not a must.
 A real interest in AI and data, and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences
 Someone who knows how to use AI tooling well to move faster and work more efficiently across research, analysis and drafting, without compromising on quality
 Seriously organised, good with detail, and able to keep several things moving at once
 Excellent writing, especially to a deadline, including executive-level materials
 Good commercial instincts: you can uncover a customer's challenge and help build the case for how AI addresses it
 The ability to earn trust and build strong working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders
 Plenty of energy, comfort with ambiguity and pace, and no job feels beneath you
 You care about what AI could do for government, public services and industry

 UK public sector procurement, frameworks or tenders
 Experience selling or supporting AI products or services
 Comfortable with CRM and performance reporting tools
 A technical or analytical background

 You'd be in at the very start of Scale's UK business, as a founding member of the team. jobs.title: Data Scientist III
jobs.description:
Do you enjoy solving complex, ambiguous problems with data and turning insights into business impact? Amazon is looking for a Data Scientist III to join a team where your analytical expertise will directly shape strategy and drive measurable outcomes. In this role, you will lead the design and delivery of data science solutions across large-scale projects, working with cross-functional partners to unlock new opportunities. You will bring broad expertise in machine learning, statistics, and scientific research to recommend the right approaches, build actionable models, and influence how your team tackles its most important challenges. If you are a collaborative, curious problem-solver who thrives on turning data into decisions, we want to hear from you.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead the design, implementation, and delivery of data science solutions for complex or ambiguous business problems, selecting appropriate machine learning and statistical methods to maximize impact.
- Build, train, and evaluate machine learning models (e.g., classification, regression, clustering) using tools such as Python, R, and SQL, and apply advanced techniques including generative AI where appropriate.
- Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business questions into rigorous analytical frameworks, and communicate findings that influence team and organizational strategy.
- Drive data science best practices and set standards for your team, including reviewing analyses, data modeling processes, and results produced by peers, and providing constructive feedback.
- Mentor and develop other data scientists in your organization, share knowledge of emerging methods and techniques, and contribute to internal enablement through presentations and documentation.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing experiment results or refining a model you have been iterating on, then join a working session with engineers and product partners to align on how your analysis will inform an upcoming launch. After lunch, you could be exploring a new dataset, prototyping a novel approach, or writing up findings for a broader audience. Throughout the day, you will balance hands-on technical work with mentoring teammates and collaborating across groups to ensure your solutions address real business needs.
About the team
Our team is passionate about using data science to solve meaningful problems at Amazon scale. We value collaboration, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to building solutions that are rigorous, reproducible, and actionable. Whether you are developing new models, mentoring colleagues, or partnering with stakeholders to shape strategy, you will be part of a group that invests in your growth and celebrates creative problem-solving. We are focused on building an inclusive environment where every voice contributes to our shared mission. - Master's degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, business analytics, economics, finance, engineering, or computer science

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Pricing Science
jobs.description:
Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions Amazon makes, and the science behind it needs to be causally rigorous, not just predictive. The P2 Optimization Science team builds the machine learning (ML) systems that power Amazon's pricing decisions at scale: demand lift models, customer lifetime value (LTV) frameworks, and the experimentation infrastructure that validates whether pricing changes actually work.
We're looking for a Research Scientist to own causal inference at the intersection of ML and pricing experimentation. Our team has identified a real gap: the methodological bridge between econometric analysis and production-scale ML pipelines needs a practitioner who lives in both worlds. You'll build conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation models, design analysis workflows for pricing experiments, and develop reusable causal ML infrastructure that the broader team — including non-ML scientists — can rely on. If you're a scientist who wants to tackle hard causal identification problems in a high-stakes production environment, and who finds satisfaction in making rigorous methods accessible to a broader team, this role is for you.
Key job responsibilities
- Design, train, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end causal ML pipelines for pricing use cases, including CATE estimation models and heterogeneous treatment effect frameworks.
- Serve as the team's causal ML methodology expert — defining identification strategies, model selection criteria, evaluation standards, and the tradeoffs between econometric and ML approaches to causal estimation.
- Contribute causal analysis methodology to pricing A/B test post-analysis and build reusable tooling that economists and other non-ML scientists can adopt without requiring deep ML expertise.
- Assess emerging causal inference methods (e.g., synthetic difference-in-differences, generalized random forests, causal representation learning) for applicability to Amazon's pricing context, and author internal methodology proposals for adoption.
- Partner with senior economists on identification strategy and causal assumptions, collaborate with software and data engineering partners on production deployment, and align with product managers on experiment design requirements.
A day in the life
Your work directly shapes the prices customers see on hundreds of millions of Amazon products. In a given week you might investigate an optimization anomaly in simulation and trace it to an unmodeled market dynamic, then design an offline evaluation framework to benchmark competing approaches before committing to online testing. You'll collaborate with senior economists on identification strategy for a pricing experiment, present a science proposal for incorporating a new competitiveness signal into an optimization system, or work with the experimentation platform team on randomization design. You'll also have opportunities to write up novel scientific findings for submission to venues such as KDD, NeurIPS, or the ACM Conference on Economics and Computation.
About the team
The P2 Optimization Science team sits at the center of Amazon's pricing decisions. We build the ML systems, causal inference pipelines, and experimentation infrastructure that determine how prices are set across Amazon's global catalog. Our team brings together research scientists, economists, and engineers who collaborate closely to turn rigorous methodology into production-quality systems with measurable business impact. We value scientific rigor, clear communication across disciplines, and a culture where every team member's work is designed to be extensible and useful beyond their own project. If you want your science to directly influence how hundreds of millions of customers experience Amazon, this is the team to join. - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of quantitative field research experience
- Experience investigating the feasibility of applying scientific principles and concepts to business problems and products
- Experience analyzing both experimental and observational data sets - Knowledge of R, MATLAB, Python or similar scripting language
- Experience with agile development

- In depth familiarity with the literature and practice of operations management, supply chain management, inventory management, revenue management, forecasting, and/or logistics

jobs.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (Model Customization and Optimization)
jobs.description:
As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (Senior FDE) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you are the technical lead embedded inside a strategic customer, accountable for building, optimizing, and running the custom generative AI models at the heart of their business. You set the technical direction for model customization and optimization engagements, deciding what to build, how to measure it, and how it reaches production. You combine the technical depth of an AWS senior engineer with the urgency of a startup builder, using your judgment and ownership to deliver measurable business outcomes in quality, latency, and cost. 
Senior FDEs work on the hardest problems where models meet systems: building domain foundation models, post-training frontier-scale open-weight models with reinforcement learning, and migrating large training and inference workloads onto AWS Trainium. They take on problems where the business problem itself is ambiguous, define the approach, and break it into workstreams others can own. They make long-term architectural trade-offs, balance customer urgency against sustainable design, and are trusted by customer engineering leadership as a technical peer. They raise the bar for the team through design reviews, code reviews, mentorship, and hiring, and they shape how AWS builds. 
Key job responsibilities
Lead the technical engagement: Embed with the customer as the technical lead for their model customization and optimization program, spanning multiple workstreams. Partner with customer engineering and product leadership to frame the business problem, define success metrics and the evaluation bar, and set technical roadmap that moves from proof of value to production. Communicate trade-offs, risks, and results clearly to executives and engineers alike. Requires up to 25% travel. 
Define the customization strategy: Decide the right path to the customer's quality, latency, and cost targets — prompting, distillation, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (including RL with verifiable rewards and multi-turn agentic RL), continued pre-training, task-specific adapters, or building a domain foundation model. Own the data strategy, synthetic data generation, and evaluation methodology that make those decisions defensible, and drive them to production for patterns such as coding agents, vertical foundation models, and multi-adapter serving. 
Architect training and inference systems at scale: Design distributed training and RL post-training systems for large dense and mixture-of-experts models using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl, and production inference architectures using engines such as SGLang and vLLM. Architect RL interaction harnesses using frameworks such as NeMo Gym and OpenEnv, defining how agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions connect to training and evaluation. Set parallelism, precision, and serving strategies that balance throughput, latency, memory, reliability, and cost per token, and ensure the designs hold up under production load. 
Lead optimization on AWS AI chips: Lead migrations of training and inference workloads to AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Diagnose performance and accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, direct kernel-level optimization where it matters, and work with AWS Neuron and service teams to close capability gaps. Turn benchmark evidence into recommendations that shape customer infrastructure and capacity decisions. 
Lead, mentor, and raise the bar: Provide technical leadership to a team of FDEs and scientists on the engagement, breaking ambiguous problems into well-scoped workstreams and unblocking others. Mentor FDE IIs on model systems design and production ownership. Lead design reviews, provide high-judgment code review, and actively participate in hiring and interviewing. 
Multiply impact across AWS: Identify patterns across engagements and turn them into reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and reference architectures adopted by other teams. Influence the roadmaps of AWS services, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron, with field evidence. Identify and shape opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer and across similar customers. 
Oversee engagement execution: Own the delivery plan, set milestones, track progress against deadlines, and ensure the quality and completeness of all deliverables. Hold yourself and the team accountable for commitments made to the customer, escalate risks early, and adjust scope or resources when timelines are at risk. 
About the team
Team
The Custom Models & Optimization team, part of the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering team, partners with enterprises, AI-native startups, and foundation model providers to build, customize, and optimize generative AI models at scale. Our work spans domain foundation models, post-training of open-weight models, and moving training and inference onto AWS Trainium. As embedded engineers within the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering motion, we bring deep model and optimization expertise to customers' most strategic AI workloads, and we turn what we learn into tooling and patterns that scale across AWS.

 Lakebase gives customers a unified, governed foundation for operational workloads and AI-native applications , helping them move away from a fragmented estate of point databases toward a modern, scalable, serverless Postgres service. If you want to be at the forefront of operational databases for AI and intelligent applications at one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world, this is your opportunity.
 The impact you will have:  
 Drive new Lakebase revenue by identifying, qualifying, and driving Lakebase activations and consumption within a defined territory, in partnership with regional Account Executives and the broader account team
 Lead with outcomes for key Lakebase personas, including platform teams and developers , data teams , and central IT, articulating how Lakebase helps them ship features faster, simplify operational data architectures, and improve governance and cost efficiency
 Sell the value of fully-managed Postgres for intelligent applications , positioning Lakebase as the optimal choice for operational workloads that power real-time, AI-driven experiences
 Run complex sales cycles from discovery and value hypothesis through commercial negotiation and close, navigating executive, technical, and line-of-business stakeholders
 Orchestrate proof-of-value and POCs that validate Lakebase’s benefits for OLTP-style workloads, reverse ETL, and AI/ML-driven applications, in partnership with solution architects and specialists

 Enable the field by sharing Lakebase best practices, success stories, and sales motions with broader sales teams, helping scale Lakebase proficiency across the organisation
 What success looks like in this role: 
 This role requires the ability to operate across two key motions simultaneously:
 Establish top strategic focus accounts by engaging application development teams to create net-new intelligent applications leveraging Lakebase
 Drive longer-term Postgres standardisation and migration within Databricks' most strategic accounts
 Success in this role requires strength in four areas:
 Business ownership: Operate at a business-unit level by tracking revenue, pipeline, and key observations, and by identifying areas needing additional focus or support.
 Strategic account engagement: Partner with account teams to engage priority accounts, driving strategic opportunities from initial engagement through successful outcomes.
 Field, account, & customer enablement: Align customers and the field on the value of Lakebase by equipping AEs and SAs with the messaging and execution motions needed to confidently own accounts without specialist intervention.
 Market voice and thought leadership: Develop an internal and external presence, and by representing Databricks at key first- and third-party events.
 The interview process is designed to evaluate candidates across all four of these dimensions.

 Relevant enterprise sales experience , consistently exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder deals
 Proven success selling data platforms, operational databases (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, cloud-native DBaaS), or adjacent data/AI infrastructure to technical buyers and business leaders
 Strong understanding of modern data and application architectures , including cloud-native services, microservices, event-driven systems, and how operational data underpins AI and analytics strategies
 Ability to sell to both technical stakeholders (developers, architects, data engineers) and business stakeholders (product leaders, operations, line-of-business owners)
 Demonstrated experience leading specialist or overlay motions , working jointly with core Account Executives to create and progress opportunities
 Executive presence with the ability to whiteboard architectures , lead C-level conversations, and build trust with senior decision makers
 Strong value selling skills: adept at discovering pain, building a business case, and tying technical capabilities to clear, quantified outcomes
 Excellent communication, storytelling, and negotiation skills, with comfort presenting to both large and small audiences
 Bachelor’s degree

jobs.description:
GAQ327R264 
 At Databricks Information Technology, we are a product-led organization transforming the way we work, from how easy it is to use our IT services to the applications we develop to help us scale seamlessly amid incredible growth.
 As a Software Engineer, Infrastructure , you will be a core technical contributor on the IT CorpEng Infrastructure team, owning and driving the evolution of our core infrastructure and observability platforms. This role requires a strong software engineering mindset, deep technical breadth across SRE and infrastructure worlds, and the ability to deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for currently "immature" system problems. You will be responsible for building resilient, scalable, and automated infrastructure that empowers our development teams. As a member of the team, you will bridge the gap between software engineering and systems architecture, ensuring our AWS environment is cost-optimized, secure, and highly available.
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Automate: Develop and deploy production-grade infrastructure on cloud platforms (AWS preferred) using Infrastructure as Code tools like Terraform or Pulumi.
 Orchestration: Deploy, manage, and scale containerized workloads using Kubernetes (EKS/AKS), focusing on security, reliability, and resource efficiency.
 CI/CD Excellence: Build and maintain robust deployment pipelines using GitHub Actions, including both cloud-hosted and self-hosted runners for specialized build requirements.
 Drive "Observable by Default" Frameworks: Implement infrastructure standards to ensure new internal applications are secure, with logging, metrics, and tracing configured out of the box.
 Tooling, Scripting & AI: Build internal CLI tools, AI-assisted workflows, and automation scripts to streamline developer workflows and reduce manual toil.
 Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, and Support teams to execute technical projects aligned with business outcomes.
 Document & Knowledge Share: Participate in peer code reviews, maintain operational playbooks/failure triage guides, and help onboard team members onto platforms you maintain.
 What We Look For 
 Software Engineering Expertise: 3+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and tooling (required).
 Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Solid working knowledge of Terraform (modules, state management) or Pulumi (preferred).
 Cloud & Containerization: Hands-on experience building and supporting production workloads in AWS (or Azure/GCP), along with Kubernetes and Docker fundamentals.
 CI/CD & Automation: Practical experience designing, maintaining, and troubleshooting pipelines using GitHub Actions or similar modern CI/CD tools.
 Observability Foundations: Practical understanding of observability pillars (logging, metrics, tracing) and hands-on experience integrating tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana.
 Independent Execution: Proven ability to own end-to-end tasks with guidance from Tech Leads, breaking down broader technical goals into actionable technical solutions.

jobs.description:
P-1411 
 Note: this is a hybrid role and requires ~3 days in the office in São Paulo-SP. 
 Mission  
 As a Staff Data & AI Technical Solutions Engineer, you will personally drive and mentor others in producing Data & AI technical solutions for any issues reported by customers - including deep diving into production data pipelines, AI workflows, streaming data ingestion, and more.  You have deep expertise in Data & AI architectures, having seen a broad set of use cases and successfully maintained complex production environments while adhering to SLA’s. You collaborate effectively with other teams, such as product engineering and customer account teams, to deliver results for customers, especially during critical production downtime situations. You provide customers with the guidance, knowledge, and expertise to build performant architectures and reliable services to achieve their strategic objectives using Databricks’ platform. Reporting to a TSE manager, you are a technical expert within a world-class global support engineering organization, recognized for your leadership, technical depth, and ability to troubleshoot even the most complex customer situations.

 Be directly responsible for leading and driving technical solutions for a breadth of complex problems reported by Databricks customers, including escalated and critical scenarios.
 Deep Dive into code-level analysis and systems architecture of customer workloads to address issues related to Databricks products - including Spark core internals, Spark SQL, Delta, DLT, and Model Serving.
 Serve as a customer support advisor - be able to diffuse escalations during incidents directly with customer stakeholders, quickly find mitigations and solutions for advanced use cases, and be strategic at helping prevent future customer issues.   
 Help make the Databricks products simpler to use and customer production environments more stable, such as by influencing Engineering and Backline Support teams to identify areas for product improvements. 
 Be known as a deep technical expert and leader in the Databricks platform and productionizing systems, and mentor others in those areas to spread your knowledge.

 Minimum of 8 years of experience in designing, building, testing, and maintaining data pipelines. Relevant past Spark experience is mandatory.
 Expertise in SQL databases or data warehouses (such as Oracle, Teradata, SQL Server, MySQL) and ETL technologies (such as Informatica, DataStage, Talend, Fivetran).
 5 years of hands-on experience in developing two or more Big Data technologies, such as Spark & Hadoop, Lakehouse architecture - such as Delta, Data Ingestion, Data Streaming applications, or ML/AI applications for industry use cases.
 Around 3 years of hands-on experience as a technical lead on a Data & AI Engineering team, serving as the go-to person to resolve critical issues.
 Prior Support or customer-facing experience is not required for this role, but proven ability to influence cross-functionally is, such as with internal stakeholders or engineering teams.

 Technical degree or Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related field/experience

jobs.title: Team Lead - Platform Monitoring Engineer
jobs.description:
Team Lead - Platform Monitoring Engineer
 We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Team Lead to shape the future of platform observability and proactive customer monitoring. This is a high-impact technical role for someone who thrives at the intersection of platform reliability, incident response, and customer obsession.
 The successful candidate will balance technical depth with people leadership: driving monitoring solutions, alerting mechanisms, and customer-focused incident detection tools, and raising the bar of the engineers around them. You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering teams to investigate and resolve incidents, drive root cause analyses, and champion solutions that improve customer reliability and stability of the Databricks Platform.
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Technical Leadership

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL GET TO:

 - Build and deliver tailored demos and proof of concepts across Snowflake's full data platform: data engineering (Snowpark, Dynamic Tables, Snowpipe), AI/ML (Cortex AI, ML model registry), and data sharing (Data Clean Rooms, Marketplace listings)
